'''Allan Stuart Hay''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (July 23, 1929 – August 14, 2017)<ref name="OH"/><ref name="Obituary">{{cite news|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/edmontonjournal/obituary.aspx?pid=186480671|title=Allan Stuart Hay|work=Edmonton Journal|date=August 25, 2017}}</ref> was a Canadian [[chemist]], and Tomlinson Emeritus Professor of Chemistry at [[McGill University]]. He is best known for his synthesization of [[Poly(p-phenylene oxide)|Polyphenylene Oxide]], leading to the development of [[Noryl]] and various other plastics.<ref name="McGill">{{cite web|title=Memorial Tribute – Allan S. Hay (1929–2017)|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/chemistry/channels/news/memorial-tribute-allan-s-hay-1929-2017-275483|date=October 11, 2017|website=McGill University|accessdate=1 March 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
Hay graduated from the [[University of Alberta]] with a B.Sc. in 1950 and an M.Sc. in 1952, and from the [[University of Illinois Chicago]] with a Ph.D. in 1955.<ref name="OH"/>

He was a research chemist, and manager at [[General Electric]], from 1955 to 1988. In 1975, he became adjunct faculty at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].<ref name="OH">{{cite web|author=Center for Oral History| title= Allan S. Hay |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/hay-allan-s|website= [[Science History Institute]] }}</ref><ref name="transcript">{{cite book|first1= Leonard W. |last1=Fine|first2= George |last2=Wise |title=Allan S. Hay, Transcript of an Interview Conducted by Leonard W. Fine and George Wise at Schenectady, New York on 24 July 1986 |date=24 July 1986 |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/sites/default/files/hay_as_0057_suppl.pdf|place=Philadelphia, PA|publisher=[[Science History Institute|Chemical Heritage Foundation]] }}</ref>

In 1987, after retiring from GE, he became a research professor of polymer chemistry at [[McGill University]] in [[Montreal, Quebec]], Canada. Hay held the GE/NSERC Chair of Polymer Chemistry from 1987 to 1995, and the Tomlinson Chair in Chemistry from 1997 to 2014. He retired from McGill in 2014, returning to [[Niskayuna, New York]].<ref name="McGill"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 1981, Hay was named a fellow of the [[Royal Society]] of London. In 1984 he received the [[IRI Achievement Award]] from the [[Industrial Research Institute]] in recognition for his contributions to science and technology, and society generally, for discoveries in polymerization by oxidative coupling. In 1985
he received the [[Chemical Pioneer Award]] from the [[American Institute of Chemists]]<ref name="transcript"/> and in 1987 he received an honorary Doctor of Science degree from the University of Alberta.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Memorial Tribute – Allan S. Hay (1929–2017)|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/chemistry/channels/news/memorial-tribute-allan-s-hay-1929-2017-275483}}</ref>
